original_jd_summary: Laboratory Technician (Grade 1) - Biochemistry role at Melbourne Pathology's high-throughput Heidelberg facility (15,000+ daily specimens). Full-time permanent position within Australian Clinical Labs network, processing routine and specialised biochemical analyses using automated chemistry analysers. Rotating shift roster with early/late shifts and weekend work. 12-week structured orientation with mentoring for recent graduates.

As part of Australian Clinical Labs (ASX: ACL), we operate with values of inclusivity, collaboration, and professional excellence, supporting ongoing professional development and career advancement for our staff.
company_context.culture: Collaborative, inclusive environment within a high-throughput facility at Heidelberg. Culture emphasizes team-based working with mentorship from experienced scientists and technicians, supporting work-life balance through shift flexibility. Staff are encouraged to participate in laboratory meetings, continuing professional development, and career pathway progression from Grade 1 through to Senior Technician roles.
recent_news: Processing 15,000+ specimens daily across multiple disciplines at high-throughput Heidelberg facility
Part of ASX-listed Australian Clinical Labs (ACL) — national network expansion
Investment in automated instrumentation including Roche cobas and Abbott Architect platforms

Strategic focus is on quality accreditation (NATA/ISO 15189), employee retention and development through structured training, and supporting emerging diagnostic technologies including molecular pathology and advanced testing platforms.

role_details.overview: Laboratory Technician (Grade 1) - Biochemistry is an excellent opportunity for a recent graduate to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced clinical pathology environment within one of Australia's leading pathology providers. You will work as part of a collaborative team performing routine and specialised biochemical analyses on patient specimens at the Heidelberg facility, a high-throughput laboratory processing 15,000+ specimens daily. The role offers comprehensive on-the-job training and mentoring from experienced scientists and senior technicians, with a genuine pathway for career development within the national Australian Clinical Labs network.
key_responsibilities: Receive, sort, and process patient specimens (blood, urine, and other body fluids) in accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs), verifying specimen identification, labelling, and integrity prior to analysis
Operate and perform routine maintenance on automated chemistry analysers, including Roche cobas 8000 modular analyser series and Abbott Architect ci16200

Perform routine biochemistry testing including electrolytes, liver function tests (LFTs), renal function, lipid profiles, glucose, cardiac markers, thyroid function, and tumour markers; process urgent (STAT) specimens within required turnaround times

Perform internal quality control (IQC) procedures at the beginning of each shift and at designated intervals throughout the day; review QC results against Westgard rules and escalate out-of-range results to the Senior Scientist or Laboratory Manager

Participate in External Quality Assurance (EQA) programs, including RCPA Quality Assurance Programs (RCPAQAP); document all QC failures, corrective actions, and instrument flags in accordance with laboratory policy

Enter, verify, and validate patient results in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS); ensure accurate transcription and data entry of results for manual tests; identify and flag critical results for immediate notification to requesting clinicians

Adhere to all workplace health and safety (WHS) policies and procedures, follow infection control and biohazard handling protocols, maintain a clean and safe working environment, and comply with NATA (National Association of Testing Authorities) accreditation requirements and the National Pathology Accreditation Advisory Council (NPAAC) standards

Participate in laboratory meetings, training sessions, and continuing professional development (CPD) activities; assist with stock management, reagent preparation, and inventory control; support other laboratory sections during periods of high workload as directed
role_details.success_metrics: Success in this role is measured by: accuracy and integrity in specimen handling and data entry (zero critical errors), timely processing of STAT specimens within turnaround time standards, consistent performance of QC procedures per Westgard rules with documented compliance, safe working practices and adherence to WHS/biohazard protocols, effective communication of critical results to clinicians, active participation in professional development activities, and demonstrated teamwork and collaboration with laboratory team members.

required_qualifications: Bachelor of Science (Biomedical Science, Biochemistry, Medical Laboratory Science, or closely related discipline) from a recognised Australian or equivalent institution
Demonstrated understanding of basic laboratory practices, including pipetting techniques, specimen handling, and laboratory safety
Basic knowledge of quality assurance and quality control principles in a laboratory setting
Strong attention to detail and ability to work accurately under pressure
Good written and verbal communication skills
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook)
Willingness to participate in a rotating roster, including occasional weekend and public holiday shifts
Satisfactory National Police Check (conducted by Melbourne Pathology at no cost to the candidate)
Evidence of immunisation status, including Hepatitis B serology, in accordance with the Health Care Worker Immunisation Guidelines
Proof of Australian citizenship, permanent residency, or valid work rights in Australia
Satisfactory completion of a three-month probationary period
preferred_qualifications: Previous laboratory experience in a clinical pathology, research, or university teaching laboratory setting (note: laboratory experience is preferred but not essential for recent graduates)
Familiarity with automated chemistry analysers (e.g., Roche cobas, Abbott Architect, Siemens Atellica)
Experience using a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
Understanding of medical terminology and common biochemistry test panels
cultural_fit_attributes: Commitment to professional excellence and quality in diagnostic testing
Collaborative mindset with ability to work effectively in fast-paced team environments
Willingness to embrace ongoing professional development and career progression
Strong safety culture awareness and commitment to laboratory compliance
Flexibility and adaptability to shift-based work schedules and workplace demands
Initiative and problem-solving ability under pressure with high specimen volumes

company_strengths: Leading pathology provider across metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria (part of ASX-listed Australian Clinical Labs network)
High-throughput facility with modern automated analysers (Roche cobas 8000, Abbott Architect ci16200) — exposure to industry-leading diagnostic platforms
Structured 12-week orientation and competency-based training program with dedicated mentoring from Senior Scientists and Laboratory Managers
Inclusive culture and demonstrated career progression pathways — progression opportunities to Grade 2 and Senior Technician roles based on competency
Support for professional registration — assistance with AIMS (Australian Institute of Medical Scientists) membership and Medical Scientist registration pathway
Access to internal training workshops and online learning platforms for continuous professional development
what_you_get.growth_opportunities: Career progression pathway from Laboratory Technician Grade 1 through to Grade 2 and Senior Technician roles based on demonstrated competency and professional development. Structured opportunities to develop technical proficiency in automated chemistry analysis, quality assurance protocols, and data management systems. Support for AIMS membership and progression toward Medical Scientist registration. Access to internal training and continuing professional development activities. Opportunity to work within Australia's largest pathology network (Australian Clinical Labs) with exposure to emerging diagnostic technologies including molecular pathology and advanced testing platforms.
challenges_to_tackle: High-volume specimen processing environment (15,000+ daily specimens) — managing time pressure and maintaining accuracy across peak periods
Rotating shift roster including early (6:00 AM - 2:30 PM) and late (1:00 PM - 9:30 PM) shifts with occasional weekend and public holiday work — balancing work-life integration with roster flexibility
After-hours on-call participation required after completion of three-month probationary period — on-call availability for urgent specimen handling and critical result follow-up
Fast-paced clinical environment with exacting quality and safety standards — performing accurately and reliably under pressure with zero tolerance for specimen handling errors or data entry mistakes

interview_preparation.likely_focus_areas: Interview will likely assess: attention to detail and accuracy in specimen handling and data entry (critical in high-volume pathology); laboratory safety knowledge and biosafety compliance (mandatory in clinical pathology); understanding of quality assurance principles and ability to perform QC procedures per Westgard rules (core technical competency); technical proficiency or willingness to learn automated chemistry analysers (Roche cobas, Abbott Architect) and LIMS systems; ability to work under pressure with high specimen volumes and maintain performance during peak periods; teamwork and communication skills with laboratory team members and clinicians; understanding of critical result escalation protocols; commitment to professional development and career progression; and understanding of shift-based work requirements (early/late/weekend roster and on-call participation).
key_themes: Specimen integrity and accuracy — zero tolerance for labelling errors or data entry mistakes in clinical testing
Quality assurance compliance — proficiency in QC procedures, Westgard rules, and external accreditation standards (NATA/ISO 15189, RCPAQAP)
Technical platform familiarity — willingness to master automated chemistry analysers (Roche cobas 8000, Abbott Architect ci16200) and LIMS systems
Safety and biosafety culture — infection control protocols, biological waste handling, WHS compliance as mandatory professional expectations
Performance under pressure — managing high specimen volumes (15,000+ daily) while maintaining accuracy and turnaround times for STAT specimens
Teamwork and communication — effective collaboration with scientists, technicians, clinicians, and collection centre staff across shift-based environment
Professional development orientation — motivation for AIMS registration, career progression, and continuous professional development engagement
